events.title: Vite 2.0 released
events.summary: Evan You released Vite 2.0 on February 16, 2021 — the first stable Vite release with an ESM-native dev server, instant hot reload, and Rollup-powered production builds.
events.about: Vite replaced webpack's slow dev startup with native ES modules — `npm run dev` in milliseconds instead of minutes for large Vue and React apps. It became the default for Vue 3, SvelteKit, and many React starters, shifting frontend tooling toward esbuild and native ESM.

narrative.whyChosen: Vite made dev-server speed a competitive requirement for JS build tools.
narrative.whyImportant: Native ESM dev mode eliminated bundling during development for most apps.
narrative.problemSolved: Webpack dev servers were painfully slow on large SPAs, hurting developer productivity.

events.title: GHC 9.0 released
events.summary: The Glasgow Haskell Compiler 9.0.1 shipped on February 4, 2021 with linear types groundwork, improved IDE support, and compiler infrastructure updates.
events.about: GHC 9.0 delivered faster compile times for large Haskell projects and continued the evolution of the compiler backend. It underpinned Haskell 2010+ development in finance, blockchain (Cardano), and research tooling.

narrative.whyChosen: GHC 9.0 modernized the compiler infrastructure behind all production Haskell.
narrative.whyImportant: Compile-time improvements kept Haskell viable for large codebases.
narrative.problemSolved: GHC 8's backend was hard to extend and slow on megaproject builds.

events.title: Pat Gelsinger returns as Intel CEO
events.summary: Intel named Pat Gelsinger CEO on February 15, 2021 — bringing back a longtime Intel engineer to lead a manufacturing turnaround.
events.about: Gelsinger pledged to restore Intel's process leadership and expand foundry services — betting the company could compete with TSMC while supplying x86 CPUs to the data center. His tenure marked Intel's most public strategy reset in decades.

narrative.whyChosen: Gelsinger's return signaled Intel's attempt to recover lost semiconductor manufacturing ground.
narrative.whyImportant: Intel's fab strategy affects global CPU supply and US chip sovereignty debates.
narrative.problemSolved: Intel had fallen behind TSMC on leading-edge process nodes.
